operations.name: Suggest options from a website
operations.agentTask: Read the website in `sourceUrl` and write three different ways to fill the ad "Hero artwork becomes a type stage". Objective: Reuse one artwork system across acquisition and brand variants. Visual rule: The visual world persists while foreground detail gives way to readable typography. Beats, in order: - 0–2.5 s: Hero art fills a composed region of the canvas. Shows Brand color, Hero artwork, Opening line. - 2.5–4.5 s: Hero foreground exits or crops away; related secondary field remains. Shows Brand color, Hero artwork, Background artwork. - 4.5–7.5 s: One headline occupies the newly quiet stage. Shows Brand color, Background artwork, Headline. - 7.5–9.5 s: Small offer or next-step statement joins the headline. Shows Brand color, Background artwork, Offer or benefit. - 9.5–12 s: Readable brand and CTA with a small art motif. Shows Brand color, Background artwork, Logo, Call to action. Use only facts the website or pages you read state. Never invent prices, discounts, dates, guarantees or claims. When a fact a field needs is missing, write a short placeholder in square brackets, such as [offer end date]. Make the three options clearly different in angle, wording and image choice. For images, choose real, large images of this brand and product: first from the page's own images (header logo, large files, feature-page screenshots), then with an image search. A social preview card (og:image, a title on a gradient) is a last resort. Give the direct URL of the image file, never a page URL, and never an image of another brand. Use an empty string when no image fits. If image search throws because no search backend is configured, tell the user in one sentence that a SerpAPI, DataForSEO or Brave key in Settings finds better images. Then take nodetool.web.screenshot of the product's feature pages instead. Save each image you consider as an asset and look at it with view_image before you offer it. Name in the option's description any image that is only a social preview card. Write `fillOptions` as a list of three objects, `fillChoice` as "" and `fillReport` as "". Each option: - value: "1", "2" or "3" - title: a name for the direction in 2 to 4 words - description: one sentence on what it emphasizes, then the first two copy lines in quotes - image: the URL of its first image, for the option card - brandColor: the brand's accent color as #RRGGBB (buttons, links, highlights), not the page background or a theme-color that is near black or white - fields: optionalShortHook (Opening line: art hook, at most 7 words); headline (Headline: message, at most 7 words); offerOrBenefit (Offer or benefit: offer, at most 7 words); cta (Call to action: cta, at most 4 words) - images: heroArt (Hero artwork: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Hero art fills a composed region of the canvas. | Hero foreground exits or crops away; related secondary field remains.); secondaryArt (Background artwork: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Hero foreground exits or crops away; related secondary field remains. | One headline occupies the newly quiet stage. | Small offer or next-step statement joins the headline. | Readable brand and CTA with a small art motif.); logo (Logo: The brand's own logo file, such as the site header logo or its icon. Shown in: Readable brand and CTA with a small art motif.) Then show the Start step with `only: ["fillChoice"]` and a one-sentence note, so the user sees just the option cards. Picking one runs `apply`, which saves the images and fills the steps.
